question: The fact that modern cars have built-in complex computer systems, cameras, sensors and geolocation technologies and are permanently connected to manufacturer or third-party vendor servers is not just a personal data protection concern, but can also undermine the safety of drivers, passengers and nearby infrastructure.

Though UN Regulations Nos 155 and 156 lay down the rules governing vehicle cybersecurity and software updates, it is the EU that is responsible for regulating remote access to car systems – including those of vehicles that are already on the market. I therefore ask: 1.

Is the Commission planning to make it mandatory to carry out independent and periodic technical audits – including for vehicles that have been type-approved and placed on the market – to verify all external connections and vulnerabilities to unauthorised external access?

What mechanisms does the Commission plan to put in place to prevent manufacturers and third-party software and cloud service providers from remotely accessing or modifying the core functions of cars without prior authorisation?

Is there agreement on the idea of establishing a unified European system of certification and continuous monitoring of the cybersecurity of connected cars, along with incident reporting obligations, remedial measures and clear rules on manufacturer liability in cases where cyber vulnerabilities cause damage or accidents?
